evidence_quotes:
If you don't detect coolant loss then you may have missed a
problem. Rerun the fuel system tests paying attention fora
exhaust smeil.
statements.reason: The fuel-system guidance for white smoke directs a rerun of fuel-system tests when coolant loss is not detected.
statements.statement: When exhaust smoke is white, the manual directs the maintainer to check the fuel system.

evidence_quotes: THEN PUT A PIECE OF PAPER IN THE LOOK AT AND SMELL IT FOR SIGNS OF UNBURNT FUEL.

It is caused by incomplete combustion of the
fuel because of low cylinder temperature.
statements.reason: The white-smoke test calls for paper in the exhaust stream to check for unburnt fuel; the manual attributes incomplete combustion to white smoke.
statements.statement: When exhaust smoke is white, the manual directs the maintainer to look for signs of unburnt fuel by testing the exhaust stream and using a piece of paper to detect incomplete combustion.

evidence_quotes: White smoke indicates fuel not being bumed in the cylinders, or possible loss of coolant to the exhaust.
statements.statement: The manual notes that white smoke may indicate fuel not being burned in the cylinders.

evidence_quotes: White smoke indicates fuel not being bumed in the cylinders, or possible loss of coolant to the exhaust.
statements.statement: The manual notes that white smoke may indicate a possible loss of coolant to the exhaust.
